title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From camping in a tent city for basketball tickets to celebrating victories with controlled bonfires, Duke University's traditions are deeply rooted in its Gothic campus and athletic spirit.

cards.title: Tenting in K-Ville
cards.subtitle: A Winter Campout for Basketball
cards.notes: Students camp in tents for weeks outside Cameron Indoor Stadium to secure tickets for the Duke-UNC game. Line monitors enforce strict occupancy rules and call random checks.
cards.short_summary: A multi-week student tent city established to secure admission to the annual home game against rival UNC.
cards.evidence_claim: Tenting has been a tradition at Duke for 40 years, with students camping in 'K-Ville' for 2-6 weeks leading up to the Duke-UNC game.
cards.source_title: K-Ville & The ARC Study Tent | Office of Undergraduate Education
cards.access_notes: The grassy area in front of Card Gym is accessible to students during the tenting season; specific rules apply to registered tenters.

cards.title: Victory Bench Burning
cards.subtitle: Post-Game Bonfire Celebrations
cards.notes: Following major basketball victories, specifically over UNC or for National Championships, students gather on the quad to burn wooden benches in a supervised bonfire.
cards.short_summary: A controlled bonfire tradition where students burn benches to celebrate significant basketball wins.
cards.evidence_claim: The A-Team burns a bench for men's and women's basketball victories over UNC and for National Championship wins, with student roles like stokers and extinguishers.
cards.access_notes: Occurs on the West Campus quads following specific major athletic victories.

cards.title: LDOC Celebration
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate End-of-Semester Festival
cards.notes: The final day of the spring semester features a massive campus-wide festival with daytime programming and a major concert organized by the Duke University Union.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale festival and concert held annually to mark the final day of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: LDOC is a major tradition featuring daytime programming, philanthropy, and a festival-like concert to celebrate the last day of classes.
cards.source_title: DUU Last Day of Classes Celebration | Duke University
cards.access_notes: The event is primarily for Duke students and takes place across various campus locations on the final day of spring classes.

cards.title: Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Finals Fuel
cards.notes: During finals week, dining halls open late to serve breakfast food to students. It is a cherished tradition for first-years at the Marketplace on East Campus.
cards.short_summary: A late-night dining event during exam periods where students gather for breakfast food and a study break.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Breakfast is a tradition hosted each semester during the exam reading period, featuring a buffet of brunch foods at the Marketplace and Great Hall.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during reading periods; free for first-years on the meal plan, others can pay with points or cash.

cards.title: The 5:00 PM Carillon
cards.subtitle: Daily Gothic Melodies
cards.notes: Every weekday at 5:00 PM, the 50-bell carillon in the Duke Chapel tower is played manually. On Fridays, the 'Dear Old Duke' alma mater is always included.
cards.short_summary: A daily musical performance from the Duke Chapel tower featuring a manual 50-bell carillon.
cards.evidence_claim: The carillon is played on weekdays at 5:00 p.m., and the Duke Alma Mater is played every Friday, a tradition started during Terry Sanford's presidency.
cards.access_notes: The music can be heard across West Campus; the recital occurs daily at 5:00 PM.

cards.title: The Cameron Crazies
cards.subtitle: The Sixth Man of Duke Basketball
cards.notes: Known for their coordinated cheers, blue body paint, and creative distractions, this student section is a defining element of the game-day experience at Cameron Indoor Stadium.
cards.short_summary: The highly energetic and organized student section for Duke basketball games.
cards.evidence_claim: The term 'Cameron Crazies' took root in 1986 to describe the raucous behavior of Duke students during home basketball games.
cards.access_notes: Access to the student section requires a student ID and often involves waiting in line or tenting.

cards.title: The Cascada Dance
cards.subtitle: A Modern Game-Day Ritual
cards.notes: During basketball games, the song 'Everytime We Touch' by Cascada triggers a specific coordinated dance and clap among students that has spread to other campus events.
cards.short_summary: A specific song and dance ritual performed by students during basketball games and university events.
cards.evidence_claim: The song 'Everytime We Touch' became a Duke tradition at basketball games, involving signature singing, clapping, and dancing.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Duke – Blue Devil Food for Thought
cards.access_notes: Performed by the student body during home basketball games and major social gatherings.

cards.title: FAC Move-In Day
cards.subtitle: High-Energy Welcome to East Campus
cards.notes: Upperclassmen known as FACs welcome new students by sprinting to cars and carrying all their belongings into dorms, creating a high-energy atmosphere for move-in.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy welcome tradition where student counselors assist first-years with moving into their dorms.
cards.evidence_claim: First-year advisory counselors (FAC) do most of the heavy lifting during move-in day, maintaining excited spirits to welcome new members of the community.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Duke – Blue Devil Food for Thought
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually on the official move-in day for first-year students on East Campus.

cards.title: The Spring Bloom
cards.subtitle: A Seasonal Campus Pilgrimage
cards.notes: Every spring, students and locals visit the Terrace Gardens to see the massive display of over 60,000 bulbs, a tradition of seasonal appreciation since the 1930s.
cards.short_summary: The annual spring blooming of tens of thousands of flower bulbs in the historic Terrace Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: The horticulture team typically plants more than 60,000 bulbs annually for spring displays in the Terrace Gardens, including a sea of tulips.
cards.source_title: Nine Facts: Sarah P. Duke Gardens
cards.access_notes: The gardens are open to the public daily; the peak bloom typically occurs in late March or April.

cards.title: The Blue Devil Nickname
cards.subtitle: A Tribute to WWI Chasseurs Alpins
cards.notes: The university's nickname was chosen by students after WWI to honor the 'les Diables Bleus,' elite French alpine troops known for their distinctive blue uniforms.
cards.short_summary: The official university moniker inspired by elite French soldiers from World War I.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Devil nickname was chosen after World War I, inspired by the 'Chasseurs Alpins' (Blue Devils) of the French Army.
cards.source_title: Duke University Traditions - The Sports Historian
cards.access_notes: The nickname and mascot are visible at all university athletic and spirit events.
